item.title: Kamakura Great Buddha Guide: Kotoku-in, Hase & Access
item.description: The serene, weathered Great Buddha of Kamakura (Kamakura Daibutsu) is one of Japan’s most iconic sights — a colossal 13th-century bronze statue of Amida Buddha sitting peacefully in the open air at Kotoku-in temple. Once housed in a great hall that was washed away by a tsunami, the 11.3-metre figure has gazed over the seaside town for some 750 years. Together with the flower-filled Hase-dera temple nearby, it anchors a wonderful half-day in the historic former capital of Kamakura, an easy and rewarding day trip from Tokyo and Yokohama.

item.title: Otaru Guide: Canal, Glassworks & Day Trip from Sapporo
item.description: A short train ride from Sapporo, Otaru is a postcard-pretty port town built on a once-booming herring and trade economy. Its centrepiece is the Otaru Canal, lined with handsome stone warehouses and Victorian-style gas lamps — impossibly romantic at dusk and magical under winter snow. The old merchant streets now brim with glassblowing studios, music-box shops, sushi counters and sake breweries. Easy to reach and full of charm, Otaru is one of Hokkaido’s most popular day trips.

item.title: Tokyo DisneySea Guide: The World's Most Beautiful Theme Park
item.description: There is only one DisneySea in the world, and it is widely considered the most beautiful theme park ever built. Where other Disney parks aim at whimsy, Tokyo DisneySea aims at atmosphere — seven elaborately themed “ports of call” arranged around a central volcanic lagoon, with a Venetian harbour, an Arabian bazaar, a mysterious Aztec temple, and a 1920s American waterfront, all rendered with a level of detail and craftsmanship that rewards simply walking around as much as riding the rides.
